title: Synthetic Checkpoint Orchestrator for Model Promotion
creator: Ethan Li
description: Build an orchestrator that automatically kicks off lightweight, deterministic 'checkpoint' evals whenever a model version is promoted in the catalog or when a tenant upgrades/pins a different model. Checkpoint evals are small synthetic probe suites derived from production traffic fingerprints and curated edge cases. The orchestrator must be budget-aware, tenant-sensitive, and able to return a concise multi-signal quality score (generation correctness, hallucination rate proxy, latency P99, token-efficiency) within a short SLAT (<= 15 minutes). The goal is fast detection of regressions introduced by version pin/upgrades and to provide deterministic, actionable signals to callers: auto-hold promotion, mark for canary, or approve.
acceptance_criteria: When a catalog model version is promoted, the orchestrator schedules a checkpoint eval within 3 minutes and returns a quality summary within 15 minutes.
When a tenant pins/requests upgrade, a tenant-scoped checkpoint is scheduled; if tenant budget or privacy policy blocks synthetic probes, an explicit skip reason is surfaced.
Multi-signal score is computed and includes at minimum: delta-accuracy, hallucination-proxy, latency P99 delta, and token cost delta.
Automated decisions: score < hold_threshold -> promotion auto-hold with reason and linked logs; score between hold and review -> create guided review card for SRE/PM with diffs.
Dashboard widgets and alert rules show regression_count, median time_to_result, and false_positive_rate; baseline false_positive_rate < 5% after 2-week calibration.
Telemetry is emitted to our observability pipeline with tags: model_version, catalog|tenant, probe_set_id, run_id.
End-to-end tests for scheduler, probe generation, and decision logic are present and pass in CI (unit + integration smoke).
Implementation has a documented rollout plan and a kill-switch to disable automated holds for 1 week without code change.
Cost cap per promotion is enforced (configurable default $12 per catalog promotion, $3 per tenant probe) and respected in tests.
implementation_steps: Define checkpoint probe format and fingerprinting rules (privacy-preserving, no raw PII).
Implement lightweight probe generator that synthesizes representative prompts from traffic histograms and curated edge-case corpus.
Build an orchestration service that listens to catalog promotion events and tenant pin changes, applies policy, and enqueues eval runs to eval-worker pool.
Create scoring module that normalizes signals and produces a single composite quality score with configurable weights.
Integrate with notifications: Console rollout UI, Slack channel, and auto-ticketing for holds.
Expose cost and budget controls per-tenant and per-catalog promotion with sensible defaults.
Add observability: run-level and probe-level logs, SLO dashboards, and alert rules.
Write end-to-end test harness using staging model catalog and synthetic tenant fixtures.
Pilot with two internal teams and one low-volume customer before broader rollout.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature flag behind 'checkpoint_orchestrator' for internal tenants only.
Phase 1: Pilot catalog promotions for non-critical models; collect FP/FN and calibration metrics for 2 weeks.
Phase 2: Enable tenant-scoped probes for customers that opt-in via Console toggle; monitor cost and privacy skips.
Phase 3: Default-on for catalog promotions with auto-hold rules active; tenant auto-hold remains opt-in unless customer-approved.
Rollback: global kill-switch and per-catalog/per-tenant disable in Console plus immediate revoke in Control Plane.
Post-launch: 30-day evaluation to tune scoring weights and thresholds based on real regressions.
notes: Design must avoid sending tenant PII to eval clusters; use hashed fingerprints and synthetic prompt expansion.
We expect many small runs rather than fewer large ones to reduce noisy signals and make failures actionable.
Work with Legal on acceptable probe heuristics for regulated customers; provide explicit opt-out.
Consider reuse of existing probe infra (probe-runner) to avoid duplication; pair with ENG-42177 for adaptive sampling.
Calibrate cost caps in the 1st pilot — conservative defaults to avoid billing surprises.
